# Instrument Integrity Checklist: Comprehensive live QuickFIX interop conversation

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the clauses that define this feature's **arms** — the forced-miss, spurious-hit and control demonstrations. Not whether an arm passes; whether the requirement that mandates it is complete, unambiguous, and falsifiable as written.
**Created**: 2026-09-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [quickstart.md](../quickstart.md) § Step 4 · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

> ⚠️ **Why this checklist exists at formal-gate depth.** This repository's dominant recorded defect is an
> instrument that reports clean because it *could not* report anything else — and it recurs **inside the
> checks written to catch it**. FR-017 and FR-018 are therefore the requirements most worth testing as
> English before anything is built.

FR-017 now opens the closed-population clause — *"THE POPULATION THIS CLAUSE RANGES OVER IS CLOSED, AND `quickstart.md` § *Step 4* IS THE ENUMERATION"* — naming Step 4's three tables plus THE COMPLETION RULE's four closed inventories, and stating that a new assertion is not subject to FR-017 **until it is added to one of them**. FR-018 carries the same pointer at `spec.md`:874 so the two requirements range over one enumeration rather than two. The open noun phrase *"every new assertion"* is retained (it is the requirement) and is now bounded rather than left open.

Non-PASS would look like a clause permitting one arm type to discharge the other, or silence on the relation; neither is the case.
- [x] CHK003 Does the spec define what makes an arm a *spurious hit* rather than a second flavour of forced miss, in terms a reviewer can apply to a proposed arm? ## Typed-Accessor Arm — the compile-time substitution

- [x] CHK009 Is the finding that **no artifact-level observable can witness a typed accessor running** recorded as a requirement-shaping constraint, with its source evidence, rather than as background? [Traceability, Spec §Clarifications] — PASS: FR-018's exception clause (`spec.md` §858-862), SC-003 (`spec.md` §1157-1162) and the typed-accessor arm row in `quickstart.md` all cite the source evidence explicitly — "§ *Clarifications* → *Session 2026-09-10 (Gate A fresh loop, round 1)*" — and state it is a **proven, dated finding**, not an assumption. Non-PASS would be a bare assertion with no session/round citation, or the constraint appearing only in `research.md`'s "✅ DECIDED" list (which the brief flags as circular self-certification for this feature) with no FR/SC pointer; neither is the case — FR-018 and SC-003 both carry it directly.
- [x] CHK010 Are the requirements for the compile-time arm specific about what must fail to compile, and about the field/message relationship that makes it fail? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003b] — PASS: `quickstart.md`'s compile-time arm row and `plan.md` § *External obligations* → the typed-accessor compile-arm row both name the exact mechanism — mutate the counterparty source so a **declared typed read** calls the message's generated per-message accessor with a field that message does **not** declare in FIX 4.4 (worked example: `NewOrderSingle::get(LastPx&)`) — and state why it fails (no generic `get` overload exists on `FieldMap`, `Message`, or either generated class). Non-PASS would be a vague "the build should fail on a bad field" with no named mechanism or example; this is a concrete, worked, engine-verified mechanism.
- [x] CHK011 Is the requirement that `typed_accessor_arm`'s value **originate in the arm's own build step** (compile definition / generated constant) stated with the negative — that a hand-written literal satisfies the announcement and attests nothing? [Completeness, Contract §C-12] — PASS: `contracts/readback-jsonl.md` C-12 states both directions explicitly — "the announced value MUST originate in the arm's own build step… a hand-written literal satisfies the announcement and attests nothing" — and `quickstart.md`'s spurious-hit table carries a full dedicated arm for exactly this fixture (write the value as a literal, remove the arm from the build) asserting the build MUST still fail, in **both** languages, with the C++/Java asymmetry stated. Non-PASS would be C-12 stating only the positive half (value must exist) with no arm forcing the literal-substitution case; the dedicated arm is present and detailed.
- [x] CHK012 Are requirements defined for the arm's **control** — that the mutant field type exists on *some* message — and is the reason given (a nonexistent type produced a cascading diagnostic that satisfied the arm while testing nothing)? [Coverage, Gap] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `quickstart.md`:265 (the COMPILE-TIME ARM row) and `plan.md`:642 (the typed-accessor compile-arm row)** — the two closed inventories the control was missing from. Both now state it as an obligation with the cascading-diagnostic reason: the mutant field type MUST exist on **some** FIX 4.4 message, declared on a message other than the mutated one; a nonexistent type produces an unknown-type diagnostic and then, cascading from it, *no viable `get` overload naming that identifier*, which satisfies the arm's match condition **while exercising no schema check at all** — and did leave the C++ arm GREEN. `tasks.md` T016 keeps its statement; it is no longer the only site.
- [x] CHK013 Is the diagnostic condition specified per toolchain, and is the failure mode for an **unrecognised** compiler defined rather than defaulted? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-003b] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `plan.md`:642** (§ *External obligations* → the typed-accessor compile-arm row, the row the item names): *"AND AN UNRECOGNISED TOOLCHAIN FAILS THE ARM CLOSED. A host toolchain for which the derivation above yields no diagnostic pattern MUST fail the arm — never default to 'the build failed', never to 'any failure is the expected one'."* The rule is tied to the precedent the item asks for — the capability-minimums row's **an absent operand is a failure, never a pass** — and is framed as the same spurious-hit hole reached by the absent-operand route rather than by loosening. `grep -ci "unrecognis\|unrecogniz"` over the bundle went 0 → non-zero.
- [x] CHK014 Are requirements clear that the arm must not be loosened to "the build failed", and is the reason stated? [Clarity, Gap] — PASS: stated repeatedly and with reasons in `quickstart.md`'s compile-time arm row ("⛔ Do **not** repair a red arm by loosening to *'the build failed'* — never merely a non-zero exit: a typo, a missing include or a wrong namespace fails the build too") and `plan.md`'s typed-accessor compile-arm row ("Loosening to 'the build failed' is the spurious-hit hole restated"). Non-PASS would be the prohibition stated once with no reason, inviting a future editor to "simplify" it away; instead the reason (a typo/missing-include false positive) is given at both sites independently.

## Falsifiability of the Guards

- [x] CHK015 For each guard the spec mandates, does a requirement state what **else** could satisfy the condition the guard watches? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018] — PASS: FR-018 mandates this as a blanket rule ("**every guard** MUST carry at least one spurious-hit arm") with its table instantiating the "what else satisfies the condition" question per guard (`spec.md` §928-943), and states **exactly one** named, proven exception (the typed-accessor runtime-invocation guard, structurally unsatisfiable, `spec.md` §858-862 / SC-003). Non-PASS would be a rule with silent, undeclared exceptions, or guards absent from the table with no explanation; the one exception here is explicit and reasoned.
- [x] CHK016 Are requirements defined for the `∅ == ∅` case — a comparator handed empty on both sides — as a rejection rather than a pass? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-018] — PASS: FR-018's table has a dedicated row ("Fidelity witness (FR-016c) | Empty intent vs empty readback… the comparator must **reject** rather than pass on `∅ == ∅`", `spec.md` §937) and `quickstart.md`'s spurious-hit table carries the matching arm ("the comparator is handed `∅` on both sides | it **rejects**; it must not pass on `∅ == ∅`"). Non-PASS would be FR-016c stating only "no readback record ⇒ fail" without addressing the specific degenerate-comparator case; both are present.
- [x] CHK017 Is the requirement distinguishing a **missing** field from a **spurious** field from a **value mismatch** stated as three separate classifications, and is the class a subset comparison cannot see called out? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006] — PASS: FR-006 (`spec.md` §572-578) enumerates the three failure classes explicitly (value mismatch, sent-but-not-reported, reported-but-not-sent) and states "A subset comparison MUST NOT be used — it cannot detect a builder emitting a field it never intended," directly calling out the spurious class. `quickstart.md`'s forced-miss table names each class by its exact status token (`value_mismatch`, `missing`, `spurious`) and marks `spurious` as "the class a subset comparison cannot see." Non-PASS would be two classes collapsed into one status, or the subset-comparison blind spot left unstated; neither applies.
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements specified for the readback file's open mode, such that stale records from a prior run cannot satisfy the current one? [Edge Case, Research §R-4] — PASS: `contracts/readback-jsonl.md` § *Transport* states the mode as a normative requirement, not merely an arm — "**Mode**: ⚠️ truncate, not append, for **each** file" — with the reasoning laid out (an appended file lets stale records satisfy the current run) and `research.md` R-4 records it as "load-bearing, not a formatting choice." Non-PASS would be the mode left as an implementation detail discoverable only through the forced-miss arm; instead the contract states it directly as a MUST.
- [x] CHK019 Is the requirement that a missing readback record yields **fail**, never **skip**, stated in both the record contract and the evidence contract without the two disagreeing? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016c] — PASS: `spec.md` FR-016c ("A message for which **no** readback record arrived MUST fail its cell") and `contracts/witness-evidence.md` W-6 ("`skip` may not be produced by a missing readback record — that is `fail`") state the identical rule from the two named artifacts, with no third wording. Non-PASS would be one artifact silent or using looser language ("should," "typically"); both use MUST/MAY-NOT-level force and agree.
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for the token `unavailable:` being rewritten to `skip:` by the status parser — i.e. is the hard-failure-becomes-silent-skip hazard specified rather than discovered? [Coverage, Gap] — PASS: FR-024 (`spec.md` §938-940) states this as a specified hazard, not a discovered one: "The hello-gate failure MUST NOT be phrased in the `unavailable:` vocabulary: `parse_gtest_status` greps `unavailable: .*`… so reusing the idiom already in that file silently converts a stale peer failure into a skip — precisely the collapse FR-016a exists to prevent, reached by imitation rather than carelessness." Non-PASS would be this hazard appearing only as a post-hoc finding in `plan.md`'s review log; instead it is a forward-looking MUST-clause in the FR itself.

## Counterparty-Side Arm Requirements (parent repo)

- [x] CHK021 Are the requirements binding the **parent-repo** counterparty applications stated with the same normative force as the library-side ones, given that Gate A/B operate on the library PR and parent-side C++/Java gets no reviewer by default? [Coverage, Plan §Structure Decision] — PASS: `plan.md` § *Structure Decision* states the consequence explicitly ("Gate A/B operate on the library PR. The parent-side counterparty changes need an explicit review disposition — they are C++ that no Gate B reviewer sees by default") and the arm requirements themselves (FR-003b, FR-018, the typed-accessor compile-arm row) are written as MUST-clauses naming the exact parent-repo files (`interop_counterparty_main.cpp`, `InteropCounterparty.java`, their build files) with the same force as library-side FRs. Non-PASS would be the parent-side obligations left as prose suggestions while library-side ones use MUST; both use MUST, and the asymmetric-review risk is named rather than hidden.
- [x] CHK022 Is the requirement that the counterparty build's arm **gate the publish** accompanied by an explicit statement of what it does *not* cover — that `publish-counterparties.yml` is `on: push: main`, so the verdict lands after merge and is not a check on any pull request? [Clarity, Plan §Structure Decision] — PASS: `plan.md` § *Structure Decision* consequence 3 states this residual explicitly and repeats it at the typed-accessor compile-arm row: "the verdict arrives at counterparty-**publish** time — before 089's CI, and **not on any pull request**… Do not read 'gates the publish' as PR-time coverage." Non-PASS would be a bare "the arm gates the publish" claim with the PR-time gap left implicit; instead the gap is stated twice, verbatim, as a warning against the exact misreading.
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements defined for the QuickFIX-J charset assertion such that a reader knows why `value_b64` is only reconstructible with it? [Completeness, Plan §External obligations] — PASS: `plan.md` § *External obligations* row for `InteropCounterparty.java` states both the assertion and the reason: "Assert `org.quickfixj.CharsetSupport.getDefaultCharset()` is **ISO-8859-1** at startup and fail loudly otherwise. `value_b64` is only reconstructible because that charset is a total bijection over all 256 byte values; under a non-bijective charset the raw bytes are unrecoverable at application level." Non-PASS would be the assertion stated with no rationale, leaving an implementer free to "fix" the charset; the bijection argument is explicit.
- [x] CHK024 Are the requirements for all **three** emitters stated as one contract, rather than as a two-emitter contract with fixpp added by reference? [Consistency, Contract §C-7] — PASS: `contracts/readback-jsonl.md` opens with a dedicated section "⛔ THE THREE EMITTERS — the population every clause in this contract binds" naming all three by file path and stating "Every clause in this contract binds all three," and explicitly **deletes** a prior "blanket remap" shape that added fixpp by reference/synonym ("An earlier revision said 'wherever this contract says both emitters it means all three'… The remap is deleted. Each clause names the population it binds."). Non-PASS would be exactly the deleted shape; the contract records having found and removed it.
- [x] CHK025 Is the requirement that the cross-language fixture be **extended** rather than replaced when the third emitter lands stated where the implementer will read it? [Clarity, Gap] — PASS: `tasks.md` T040 states it directly, in the task an implementer executes: "Extend the cross-language golden fixture at `phase-9-harness/interop-readback-fixture/` from **two** emitters to **all three**… ⛔ **Extend it, do not replace it** — the committed two-way half carries a re-derivation recipe and a proven can-it-fail check (C-7 · FR-004)." The "two-way" fixture is inherited from a named parent commit (`tasks.md` §40, parent `counterparty-rebuild` at `0aa5cf0`), which resolves what "when the third emitter lands" refers to. Non-PASS would be silence on extend-vs-replace, risking a from-scratch fixture that discards the already-proven QuickFIX-cpp/QuickFIX-J half; T040 forbids exactly that.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK026 Does any requirement still describe an arm whose observable is unstated, after the round that removed two such arms? [Ambiguity, Quickstart §Step 4] — PASS: re-scanned every row of `quickstart.md`'s forced-miss, spurious-hit and controls tables; every `Expect`/observable cell names a concrete, checkable difference (a status token, a byte value, a diagnostic shape, an equality result) — none reads as a bare "fails" or "passes" with no named discriminant. Non-PASS would be finding a row whose Expect column is generic (e.g. "the guard fires") with no named value/diagnostic; none was found.
- [x] CHK027 Are the terms *forced miss*, *spurious hit* and *control* used consistently across `spec.md`, `quickstart.md` and the three contracts, with no fourth synonym? [Consistency] — PASS: grep across all five artifacts for the term family found only hyphenation variants of the same terms (`forced miss`/`forced-miss`, `spurious hit`/`spurious-hit`, `positive control`/`positive-control`/`validator-positive-control`) — normal adjectival-vs-noun-phrase English, not competing vocabulary. No synonym like "false pass" or "vacuous pass" was found standing in for *spurious hit*. Non-PASS would be a fourth term doing the same job under a different name; the one organizational inconsistency found (a control-labelled row filed in the forced-miss table) is a placement defect, captured separately at CHK007, not a naming defect.
- [x] CHK028 Is "prove the instrument can report non-zero" expressed as a checkable obligation with a named artifact, or as an exhortation? [Measurability, Gap] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `plan.md`:646** — a new § *External obligations* row under RC-A/RC-B naming both the recipient and the producer: `.specify/decisions/089-quickfix-interop-conversation-verify.md`, produced by `/speckit-verify`. ⚠️ **The producer was verified to exist before being named**, rather than invented: `/speckit-verify` records already carry per-cell arm tables (`Cell | Basis | RED may be taken | Mutant`), and `tasks.md` T110 already writes to this exact path — so this is a structural pointer, not a new artifact gated with nothing behind it (which would have reproduced RC-A inside the fix for RC-A). The row states the content: one entry per arm of all three Step-4 tables, its **unmutated-tree GREEN** result, and its RED **together with the diagnostic that RED asserted**. No arm count is written into the row; the enumeration is Step 4.
